description: Known places where the SheetJS oracle output (test/corpus/expected, .cache/expected) is wrong or differs on purpose from what effect-spreadsheet must return. Tests compare against SheetJS except at these locations, where they expect `correct`. r/c are 0-based. Value formats by `field` (the same for `sheetjs` and `correct` unless noted): hiddenRows = array of row indices; ref = A1 range string; cells = array of [r, c, v] where v null means 'no cell'; dimension = `sheetjs` {ref} (SheetJS's !ref) and `correct` {cells, declaredRows, declaredCols} (the span of the cells and the declared size). expected.mjs checks every `sheetjs` value against the oracle result and every `correct` value against the fixture bytes (the `correctCheck` method), fails on a mismatch, and copies the ids into each affected expected file as `knownQuirks`.

quirks.note: F;SDM6;R1 is a row-format record without M; SheetJS keeps Mval = 0 and marks row 0 hidden (bits/40_harb.js ~563). Only F;M0;R3 hides a row.
SheetJS does not honour the FE FF BOM and reads the bytes as 8-bit text. Correct values are the decoded text (numbers stay text here: the check is on the decoded fields).
Bytes 0x80-0x9F are decoded as ISO-8859-1 (C1 control characters U+0080, U+0093, U+0094) instead of Windows-1252 (€, curly quotes).
The numeric character reference 🍣 (outside the BMP) is truncated to 16 bits: U+F363 instead of U+1F363 (🍣).
_x000D_ decodes to CR; SheetJS drops it.
Informational: an explicit empty quoted field ("") gives no cell in SheetJS; our reader may report an empty text cell there.
Informational: SheetJS's ref is the actual cell range for SpreadsheetML/SYLK, while it keeps the declared range for xlsx/xlsb/xls.
